newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair dismisses call for public spending hike.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair dismisses call for public spending hike.

text.p: British opposition Labour leader Tony Blair, promising that his party would pursue macroeconomic stability, said it was nonsense for left-wingers to argue that a Labour government must increase public spending.
Blair said the debate in Britain should be about how to use the government's annual budget of 320 billion stg rather than to argue that nothing will change unless it increases spending.

"It is surely time for the left of centre to liberate itself from this nonsense," Blair told a business conference. "No government, Labour or Tory, should practice policies of financial imprudence," he added.

Blair said Labour must set a target for low inflation and stick to it. "Government must be responsible in borrowing, sticking to the "golden rule" so that government borrowing does not exceed investment over the cycle," he said.
